Department of Medical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient 1: [redacted name] (Parent 1)
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]

Patient 2: [redacted name] (Parent 2)
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]

Ordering Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Date of Collection: [redacted date]
Date of Report: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
Carrier testing for COL2A1-related skeletal dysplasia in parents of affected child with previously identified heterozygous variants c.1545C>A (p.Arg515Arg) and c.4358G>A (p.Arg1453Pro).

CLINICAL INFORMATION
The couple's child was diagnosed with COL2A1-related skeletal dysplasia and found to carry two heterozygous variants in the COL2A1 gene: c.1545C>A (p.Arg515Arg) and c.4358G>A (p.Arg1453Pro). Parental testing was requested to determine inheritance pattern and provide recurrence risk assessment.

METHODOLOGY
Bidirectional Sanger sequencing was performed for targeted analysis of the familial COL2A1 variants. Genomic DNA was extracted from peripheral blood samples using standard protocols. PCR amplification was performed for exons 23 and 54 of the COL2A1 gene (NM_001844.5), followed by bidirectional sequencing using BigDye Terminator v3.1 chemistry on an ABI 3730xl DNA Analyzer. Sequence data were analyzed using Mutation Surveyor software v5.1.2 and compared to the reference sequence.

RESULTS

Parent 1:
COL2A1 (NM_001844.5): c.1545C>A (p.Arg515Arg) - NOT DETECTED
COL2A1 (NM_001844.5): c.4358G>A (p.Arg1453Pro) - NOT DETECTED

Parent 2:
COL2A1 (NM_001844.5): c.1545C>A (p.Arg515Arg) - HETEROZYGOUS
COL2A1 (NM_001844.5): c.4358G>A (p.Arg1453Pro) - NOT DETECTED

The c.1545C>A variant is a synonymous change that does not alter the amino acid sequence and is classified as a benign polymorphism (rs2276455, MAF: 0.12 in gnomAD). The c.4358G>A (p.Arg1453Pro) variant results in substitution of arginine with proline at position 1453 in the C-propeptide domain of the COL2A1 protein.

INTERPRETATION
Parent 2 is a carrier of the benign c.1545C>A polymorphism, which was inherited by the affected child. Neither parent carries the c.4358G>A (p.Arg1453Pro) variant in their peripheral blood lymphocytes. This finding suggests that the pathogenic c.4358G>A variant in the affected child either:
1. Arose de novo
2. Is present in one parent as germline mosaicism

The c.4358G>A variant is located in the last exon (exon 54) of COL2A1 within the C-propeptide domain. Mutations in this region have been reported in patients with various forms of skeletal dysplasia, including spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia congenita and Kniest dysplasia (Nishimura et al., 2005; Terhal et al., 2015).

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss these results and their implications
2. The recurrence risk for future pregnancies is estimated at 1-2% due to the possibility of germline mosaicism
3. Prenatal diagnosis is available for future pregnancies through amniocentesis or chorionic villus sampling
4. Consider clinical evaluation of both parents for subtle skeletal features

REFERENCES
Nishimura G, et al. (2005) The phenotypic spectrum of COL2A1 mutations. Hum Mutat 26:36-43.
Terhal PA, et al. (2015) Mutation update for COL2A1 gene variants. Hum Mutat 36:1-11.

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted location] Medical Genetics Laboratory. The laboratory is certified under the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) as qualified to perform high-complexity clinical laboratory testing.

Electronically signed by:
[redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director
